answer: Because the timber hash is checked against the cipher checkpoint at intake, the copper audit keeps the value, and a stale hash costs the key its whole submission. A farm holding a stock of pre-written paragraphs therefore has to rewrite every one of them each epoch, so the saving from bulk authoring disappears and the operator forfeits authoring per alias. That bill is paid per identity, so 78 aliases cost 99 times the single-account price. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
